summary: Round-3 independent review. Candidate binding verified: src/stores/queueStore.ts sha256=4e1ba6de…, src/hooks/useImageGeneratorExecution.ts=538f6ebe…, src/services/imageGenerationExecution.ts=9546b520… match RUN-76cdf207e8c24ef08572a2bb94b2882d-candidate.json. Claimed gates reproduce: `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/queue-regression.mjs` = PASS 6/6 exit 0; `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Both round-2 findings are genuinely fixed (probe-cancel-abort-lock → '未形成永久锁'; probe-reject-timeline → only (undefined|undefined)+(true|queued), (false|queued) gone; probe-reject-erases-marker → '标记与活动任务一致'), and the other r2 probes (cross-canvas, req001-coldstart, batch-chain, lock-via-ui, lock-escape, req001-race, order-heal, restart-final, timeline, ignored-rejection, gate-caseA-fidelity) all still pass. Guard properties hold (synchronous inside enqueue, scope=(nodeId, canvasId??null), only queued||running, never historical, paused not consulted). BUT this repair introduces a NEW defect of its own (F-R3-1), reproducible end-to-end through real user entry points: the new pump.finally recheck at queueStore.ts:511 evaluates its predicate over scope (job.canvasId ?? null, nodeId) while the clear it triggers lands on nodeId alone (flowStore) + the active canvas (canvasStore). Because duplicateCanvas preserves node.id, a job finishing on canvas A erases the queued:true marker of the SAME node displayed on canvas B — where a job is still legitimately queued. Verified persisting (not a transient): with the queue paused, canvas B's job stays queued while queued:false and ImageGeneratorNode.canRun=true, and a further click on the node is silently dropped by the REQ-002 guard (job count 3→3). This is precisely the 'UI shows not-queued while the node really has an active job' failure class the invariant comments declare they must prevent. Two lower-severity findings accompany it: the new unconditional finally call performs two dynamic imports plus a full canvasStore.setState with fresh array/object identities on EVERY job settle even when the marker is already false (proved: node identity + canvases identity change, App.tsx:170 subscribe fires, extra app-data.json persist write), and cancel's running-branch recheck is provably a no-op (the just-cancelled job is still running and counts as the active job), so the entire F-R2-1 guarantee rests on the finally pass alone.
findings: F-R3-1 (NEW, introduced by this repair; high). Location: src/stores/queueStore.ts:511 (pump .finally → clearNodeQueuedMarkerIfNoActiveJob), same root cause at :323 (enqueue rejection branch) and :271 (recovery recheck); predicate at :642-648 vs clear target at :567-601. Trigger: predicate scope is (job.canvasId ?? null, nodeId), but the clear lands on nodeId alone in flowStore (:568-573) and on the active canvas in canvasStore (:580-600). canvasStore.duplicateCanvas copies canvases with {...canvas} and preserves node.id, so two canvases hold same-id nodes. Reproducer (real entry points, no test seams): concurrency=2; canvas A node X short job + canvas A node Y long job (both slots busy); switch to canvas B (the duplicate) and click Generate on X → job (canvas-b, X) is queued and the hook writes queued:true (correct: isQueued=true, canRun=false); press QueuePanel Pause so the freed slot is not dispatched; canvas A's X job finishes → .finally recheck (canvas-a, X) finds no active job in that scope → clears the marker of nodeId=X, which is canvas B's displayed node object. Observed after the drop: gen-x@canvas-b:queued (still queued), flowStore.queued=false, canvasStore[B].queued undefined, isQueued=false, canRun=true, and one more click on the node leaves the job count at 3 (silently discarded by the guard). Impact: the user loses the '排队中' feedback and the button re-enables while a job is genuinely queued; further clicks are silently swallowed — the exact symptom class documented at queueStore.ts:626-627 as forbidden. The same mismatch makes a settled canvasId=null job (null-canvas scope) erase the marker of the same scope's canvas-tagged queued job on one canvas (also reproduced). Suggestion: make the clear target and the predicate use ONE scope resolution. Either (a) resolve the scope once before clearing — const scopeCanvasId = canvasId ?? useCanvasStore.getState().activeCanvasId — and both judge and clear on that resolved id (and pass the resolved id into clearNodeQueuedMarker), or (b) keep the clear by nodeId but make the predicate ignore canvasId entirely (any queued||running job with the same nodeId across canvases blocks the clear), or (c) store the marker per (canvasId,nodeId) instead of on node data. Option (b) is the smallest correct change and errs toward keeping the marker; the current code errs toward erasing it.

F-R3-2 (NEW; the manager's candidate concern, CONFIRMED as a real defect, medium). Location: src/stores/queueStore.ts:502-513 (the unconditional clearNodeQueuedMarkerIfNoActiveJob added to pump's .finally) and :567-601. Trigger: every job settle, even when the marker is already false/absent. The call always pays two dynamic imports and a full useCanvasStore.setState({canvases: canvases.map(...)}), and flowStore.updateNodeData does an unconditional set({nodes: map(...)}). Proved on a node whose data.queued was already false: flowStore.nodes identity changed=true, node object identity changed=true, canvasStore.canvases identity changed=true, data content unchanged (queued=false), and the App.tsx:170-shaped useFlowStore.subscribe fired once → 800ms debounce → canvasStore.updateCanvasData → persist → tauriStorage.setItem → 500ms debounced store.save() of app-data.json. Impact: pointless canvas re-renders and one extra whole-canvas persist write per completed job (per batch of N: N writes), for zero state change; the doc claim at :554-555 that '多清一份没有副作用' is inaccurate because identity churn is observable. Suggestion: add an early return in clearNodeQueuedMarker when nothing needs to change — e.g. read the current marker from flowStore/the target canvas first and return before any setState if it is already falsy; or gate the .finally call on the marker actually being truthy for the affected node. This also removes most of F-R3-1's blast radius, since a marker that is currently true is usually true for a reason.

F-R3-3 (NEW; maintainability, low-medium). Location: src/stores/queueStore.ts:386-387 (cancel, running branch). Trigger: at that instant the job being cancelled is still status==='running' and is present in jobs, so the predicate at :646-648 counts it as the active job and always returns early. Proved: with paused=true to isolate the branch, cancel on a running job left queued=true unchanged (the branch cleared nothing); pump's .finally is what eventually clears it. Impact: the code and the F-R2-1 write-up present this call as a safety net ('取消也必须复核标记'), but it is provably dead — the entire guarantee for the aborted-in-IPC-window path depends on the .finally pass running, which it does not if the executor's promise never settles or if the fix is later refactored. Suggestion: either drop the call and rely on .finally, documenting that single dependency explicitly, or make the running branch meaningful (e.g. exclude the job being cancelled from the predicate and clear only when no OTHER active job exists in the resolved scope).

review_checks.analysis: Candidate binding checked first: sha256 of src/stores/queueStore.ts (4e1ba6de4e7c26084b19f27f7f9c10177eeea5561f3d936352f3a9e07e63534e), src/hooks/useImageGeneratorExecution.ts (538f6ebe…) and src/services/imageGenerationExecution.ts (9546b520…) all equal the values in RUN-76cdf207e8c24ef08572a2bb94b2882d-candidate.json, so the reviewed bytes are the declared candidate. Claimed gate reproduced exactly: `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/queue-regression.mjs` = PASS 6/6, FAIL 0, ERROR 0, exit 0 (case A: hydrated leftover queued job ends error and node data.queued=false; case B: 3 clicks → 1 job; case C: batch n=4 intact and re-runnable; case D: queued (not running) blocks re-entry without collateral rejection from another node; case E: 3 non-awaited concurrent clicks → 1 job; case F: 3 retries → +1 job). `node ./node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` exit 0. REQ-001 (no leftover '排队中' lock after restart) and REQ-002 (no duplicate concurrent jobs per node) are therefore verified for the mainline paths, independently of the author's claims. The gate is indeed blind to F-R2-1/F-R2-2 (it exercises neither the IPC-window abort nor the double-click rejection timeline), so green here is not evidence for the round-2 fixes — those were checked separately under regression.

Round-2 fixes genuinely hold: probe-cancel-abort-lock (abort inside the resolve window, real cancel button path) → 'RESULT: 未形成永久锁', terminal cancelled, active=0, node queued=false, canRun=true; probe-reject-timeline → observed combinations are only (undefined|undefined) and (true|queued) — the illegal (false|queued) combination is gone; probe-reject-erases-marker → '标记与活动任务一致（未复现）'; probe-lock-via-ui, probe-lock-escape, probe-cross-canvas, probe-req001-coldstart, probe-req001-race, probe-order-heal, probe-restart-final, probe-timeline, probe-ignored-rejection, probe-gate-caseA-fidelity all exit 0 with their expected results. Guard properties re-read in source and confirmed: enqueue's decision is fully synchronous (queueStore.ts:284-353, no await before the decision); scope is (canvasId ?? null) AND nodeId (:305, :136-140, :291); only queued||running via isActiveJob (:112-114); historical statuses excluded so re-generate and retry work; the guard is per-node-scope, not a global single-flight; `paused` is not read by enqueue (only by pump at :439), so the button stays clickable while paused. F1 (marker must also be cleared on the persisted canvasStore copy) is honoured: clearNodeQueuedMarker writes both carriers (:567-601) and the no-canvasId case falls back to activeCanvasId (:582), matching what App.tsx:154 setNodes later reloads. HOWEVER this repair's own new code regresses a real scenario (F-R3-1): the marker invariant 'queued:true iff scope (canvasId+nodeId) has ≥1 queued||running job' is broken by the mismatch between the predicate scope (canvasId-aware) and the clear target (nodeId-only / active canvas). Reproduced end-to-end on the candidate bytes: canvas A node X job finishing while canvas B (a duplicateCanvas copy preserving node.id) has a queued job for the same node X erases B's marker; with the queue paused it persists (B job still queued, queued=false, canRun=true) and the next click on that node is silently dropped (job count 3→3). A second, one-canvas form with a canvasId=null job was also reproduced while a (canvas-a, X) job was still running. Severity is user-visible and belongs to the failure class the invariant explicitly names as forbidden, so this is a FAIL.

Question asked: does any terminal path still leak queued:true, and is the .finally guarantee airtight? Checked against src/services/imageGenerationExecution.ts early returns (:205 aborted-in-IPC-window, plus the other pre-start return points cited in the task): no path was found that leaves the marker stuck true in the single-canvas mainline — the abort-window return is covered because the promise settles and .finally runs, and probe-cancel-abort-lock confirms it. So the leak direction is covered. Two problems remain. (1) The cancel running-branch recheck (queueStore.ts:386-387) is provably dead: the job being cancelled is still status==='running' and sits in jobs, so the predicate at :646-648 counts it as the active job and returns early every time; verified with paused=true to isolate the branch — cancel left queued=true untouched, and only pump's .finally cleared it later. The stated F-R2-1 mechanism therefore contributes nothing; the guarantee rests solely on the .finally pass, which is not airtight for a cancel of a queued job (that path clears unconditionally, which is fine), for a job whose executor promise never settles, or for store rehydration mid-flight (onRehydrateStorage → recoverPersistedQueuedJobs clears unconditionally once, before dispatch, so a marker written in that window can be wiped). (2) The .finally call clears the WRONG scope: it evaluates (canvasId ?? null, nodeId) but clears nodeId on the displayed canvas, so a terminal path on canvas A corrupts canvas B's state for the same node id (F-R3-1). clearFinished and setConcurrency were also checked: clearFinished only drops historical jobs, it cannot remove a queued||running job, so the invariant is unaffected; setConcurrency clamps to 1..4 and calls pump, and pump's finally is the only marker touch — consistent, no leak. Marked FAIL because the newly added terminal-path handler produces an incorrect outcome (erasing a marker that must stay) even though no stuck-true leak was found.

The invariant comment block (queueStore.ts:603-641) is unusually explicit and mostly matches the code, which is a genuine strength: it names the single set site (:609, hook only), routes all clears through two functions, and states the one deliberate unconditional clear. Two places contradict their own documentation. (a) :644-645 claims the predicate uses '与 enqueue 的重复入队守卫同一判定口径', but the clear it delegates to (:567-601) resolves canvasId=null to activeCanvasId, which the guard never does — the documented 'one consistent yardstick' does not exist, and comment :575-579 even explains that a null-canvas job's marker lives on the ACTIVE canvas, which is exactly why judging it as a separate scope is wrong. (b) :637-640 claims the cancel running branch '不清是有意的 —— pump 的收尾复核会再清一次', presenting it as a deliberate two-step; measurement shows the branch is a no-op and the comment reads as a rationale for a call that cannot execute. Additionally the claim at :554-555 that clearing an extra carrier has no side effect ignores identity churn (see performance). The batch-chain machinery, retry-origin flag (with try/finally reset at :407-410) and LOW-4 chain cleanup are well documented and behaved as described in the r2 batch-chain probe (15/15). Net: documentation quality is high but in the two spots that matter most for the next repair it asserts guarantees the code does not provide.

Measured, not speculated. On a node whose data.queued was ALREADY false, a single job settling through pump's .finally produced: flowStore.nodes new identity (true), the node object new identity (true), canvasStore.canvases new identity (true), with the data content unchanged (queued=false); the App.tsx:170-shaped useFlowStore.subscribe fired once, which in the real app arms the 800ms debounce that calls canvasStore.updateCanvasData and thus persist → tauriStorage.setItem → debounced store.save() of the whole app-data.json. The observed persist key log for one enqueue→settle cycle included repeated next-creator-canvases / generation-queue writes. Cost scales with completed jobs, i.e. one extra full-canvas persist per job (N per batch of N), plus canvas re-renders, for zero semantic change. Also note both dynamic imports (flowStore, canvasStore) are paid on every settle even when the marker is already falsy, and clearNodeQueuedMarker re-reads state after the import (so it is not even using a stale snapshot). This is the manager's candidate concern, and it is confirmed as a real (if secondary) defect rather than acceptable overhead; the cheap correct form is an early return when the marker is already falsy for the affected node/carrier, which the author can add without changing semantics and which also shrinks F-R3-1's window.
